ORAL ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Hike in security deposit for new LPG connections 
*401. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of PETROLEUM AND 
NATURAL GAS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that the public sector oil 
companies such as Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and 
Hindustan Petroleum have stopped issuing new LPG connections; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; 
(c) whether it is a fact that the oil companies have demanded a 
security deposit hike of Rs. 250/- for each new connection after the cost 
of steel went up from Rs. 17000 per ton to Rs. 28000 per ton; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) what is Government's reaction thereto? 
THE MINISTER OF PETROLEUM AND NATURAL GAS (SHRI 
MANI SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) to (e) AStatement is laid on the Table of the 
House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) The release of new c onnections by Public Sector Oil 
Marketing Companies (OMCs) has been affected by shortage of cylinders 
due to cylinder manufacturers not honouring their commitment on 
supplies because of continuous increase in steel prices. This has resulted 
in some build-up of waiting lists of  new customers. Government have, 
therefore, directed OMCs to liquidate by mid-September the waiting list 
of LPG customers as on 1.8.2004. 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
(c) to (e) OMCs have approached the Government for an increase 
in security deposit for LPG cylinders due to hike in procurement cost 
of cylinders following increase in steel prices. The matter is under 
consideration of the Government.

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
Assistance to panchayats due to flood 
† *403. SHRI VIDYASAGAR NISHAD: Will the Minister of 
WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware that several panchayats of Gogri-
block of Khagaria in Bihar have been affected due to flood; and 
(b) what assistance has been provided by the Central Government 
to the affected panchayats so far and the steps being taken to construct 
platforms with roofs in the said panchayats? 
†The Original notice of question was received in Hindi. 
5 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYA RANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) Yes, Sir. As reported by the State Government of Bihar, 
several panchayats of Gogri-block of Khagaria district in Bihar have been 
affected by floods in July, 2004. 
(b) Flood Management being a State subject, it is the primary 
responsibility of the State Governm ent concerned for the execution of 
rescue and relief operations. The Government of India supplements the 
efforts of the State Governments, where necessary, by extending financial 
and logistic support as per the pr ovisions of the Eleventh Finance 
Commission. For this purpose, the Finance Commission has allocated 
certain amount under Calamity Relief Fund (CRF) to each State. 
Assistance for calamity of severe nature is also provided from National 
Calamity Contingency Fund (NCCF) after following the laid down procedure. 
During the current year 2004-05, besides releasing Rs.90.12 crore under 
CRF, an amount of Rs. 55 crore has been provided to the State Government 
from NCCF. 
Providing relief at the ground level comes within the purview of the 
State Government. Further, the State Government has informed that 
presently there is no such scheme either under execution or envisaged 
for construction of platforms with roofs. However, the Government of 
India has constituted a Task Force to look into the problem of recurring 
floods in various States including Bihar.

Rural and urban share in bank deposits 
*405. SHRI MOTILAL VORA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the rural and urban share in bank deposits, at present; 
(b) the amount of loans provided by banks in rural areas; 
(c) whether Government propose to provide more loans for rural 
areas; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) 
and (b) The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reported that the share of 
rural, semi-urban and urban (including Metropolitan) areas in banks' 
deposits during the year 2003- 04 was 12.86%, 17.62% and 69.52%, 
respectively. The bank credit given to the rural areas during the said 
period was Rs. 85,224 crores (approx) representing 9.56% of the total 
credit. 
(c) and (d) Pursuant to the Agriculture Credit Policy announced by 
Government on June 18, 2004, the RBI has advised all Scheduled 
Commercial Banks and NABARD to all Cooperative Banks to enhance 
agricultural credit during the year 2004-05. Keeping in view the 
Government's goal of significantly improving flow of credit and covering 
additional farmers under institutional credit, the aforesaid policy envisages 
the following measures:— 
(i) Rescheduling/restructuring loans of distressed farmers; 
(ii) One Time Settlement (OTS) for small and marginal farmers; 
(iii) Fresh finance for farmers whose earlier debts have been settled 
through compromise or write off; and 
(iv) Relief measures for farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders. 
The RBI and NABARD have issued guidelines in this behalf, on 24th 
June and 29th June 2004, respectively to Schedule Commercial Banks 
7 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
and Cooperatives. The Credit flow to Agriculture from all lending institutions 
is projected at about Rs. 1,05,000 crores. 
The above policy envisages coverage of at least 100 new farmers at 
each rural and semi-urban branch, targeting a total number of 50 lakh 
farmers throughout the country; loans for two to three investment projects 
in the new areas of plantation and horticulture, fisheries, organic farming, 
agro-processing, livestock, micro irrigation, sprinkler irrigation, watershed 
management, village ponds development and other allied activities, apart 
from financing 10 agro-clinics in every district. 
Committee for proper water management 
†*406. DR. MURLI MANOHAR JOSHI: 
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI: 
Will the Minister of WATER RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have constituted a new Committee for 
suggesting proper management of water in the country; 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and by when the said Committee is 
likely to submit its report; 
(c) whether Government had received suggestions with regard to 
proper management of water during the past years also; and 
(d) if so, the action taken thereon? 
THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYA RANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) to (d) The Government has not constituted any new 
Committee for suggesting proper management of water in the country. 
However, Ministry of Water Resources has constituted a Task Force for 
Flood Management/Erosion Control to suggest short term and long term 
measure for management of flood control in Assam and other 
neighbouring states as well as Bi har, West Bengal and Eastern Uttar 
Pradesh. The Planning Commission has also constituted (i) Task Group 
on Integration of ongoing schemes to address Water Conservation as a 
Water Mission and (ii) Task Group on Efficient utilisation of Water 
Resources. 
The suggestions on various issues relating to development and 
management of water resources are expressed by experts from time to

Farmer-friendly Credit Policy 
*407. SHRI B. J. PANDA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government propose to bring in a farmer-
friendly credit policy during the current fiscal; 
(b) if so, the details of the proposed scheme; 
(c) whether Government would grant interest-free loans to certain 
categories of poor farmers; 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) what is the action plan of Government to control suicides by 
debt-ridden farmers in the country? 
THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (S HRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) 
and (b) An announcement has already been made by the Government 
on 18.6.2004 for increasing the ground level credit flow to agriculture 
and allied activities by 30% during 2004-05 and doubling the flow in 
three years. This Farmer-Friendl y Agriculture Credit Package also 
envisages debt restructuring/resched uling and fresh loans to farmers 
affected by natural calamities, One Time Settlement (OTS) for small 
and marginal farmers, fresh finance for farmers whose earlier debts 
have been settled through compromise or write off and relief measures 
for farmers indebted to non-institutional lenders. 
Pursuant to the above announcement, Reserve Bank of India has 
already advised all scheduled commercial banks on 24.6.2004 to take 
action to implement the programme. National Bank for Agriculture and 
Rural Development (NABARD) has also issued similar guidelines to 
Regional Rural Banks and cooperatives. 
(c) and (d) The announcement does not envisage providing interest 
free loans to farmers. 
(e) In order to provide relief to farmers facing actue distress due to 
their heavy indebtedness to non-institutional lenders i.e. money lenders, 
banks have been advised to give loans to such farmers against 
appropriate collateral or groups security.

THE MINISTER OF FINANCE (SHRI P. CHIDAMBARAM): (a) to 
(c) RBI has reported that the inspection reports conducted under Section 
35 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 of banks are confidential in nature 
and hence, contents of these reports cannot be disclosed as per 
provisions of Section 34-A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. 
Reserve Bank of India (RBI), on the directions of its Board for 
Financial Supervision (BFS), has prescribed a procedure for dealing 
with divergence in assessment of non-performing assets as assessed 
by the bank and certified by the Statutory Auditors and as assessed by 
the Principal Inspecting Officers (PIO) of the RBI. Divergence is grouped 
into two headings viz. subjective and objective criteria. When the additional 
provision recommended by Principal Inspecting Officer exceeds 5% to 
the total provisions held in case of divergence arising out of objective 
parameters, or 15% to total provisions held in case of divergence arising 
out of subjective criteria, the same are termed as "significant", and the 
same are re-examined independently by another senior officer of the bank. 
In case of continued divergence, the Statutory Auditors/Management of 
the banks would have to ensure that the shortfall in the provision is made 
good in the next financial year. 
The ICICI Bank Ltd. has reported in its published documents, the gross 
NPAs at Rs. 5013.03 crore as on March 31, 2002, Rs. 5027.38 crore as on

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYA RANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) and (b) A long-term analysis of ground water levels by 
the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB), under the Ministry of Water 
Resources during the years 1983—2002 indicates decline in ground water 
levels by more than 4 meters in parts of some districts of various States 
of the country. The names of the States/districts having pockets of 
declining water level in the last twenty years (1983—2002) are given in 
the Statement (see below) 
(c) In order to check receding of ground water level, the following 
measures have been suggested:— 
(i) Ground water resources augmentation through rain water 
harveting and artificial recharge to ground water. 
(ii) Regulation of ground water development through notification 
and legislation. 
(d) Water being a State subject, it is primarily the responsibility of 
the concerned State Governments to plan, finance and execute schemes 
for augmenting water resources. The Central Government has initiated 
18 

[24 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
following measures to check over-exploitation of ground water:— 
(i) Implementation of a Central Sector Scheme for Study of Recharge 
to Ground Water in the country. 
(ii) Circulation of Manual/Guidelines on Artificial Recharge of Ground 
Water to the States/Union Territories to enable them to formulate 
area specific artificial recharge schemes to check the declining 
trend of ground water levels. 
(iii) Circulation of a Model Bill in the year 1970 which was re-circulated 
in 1992 and again in 1996 to all the States/Union Territories to 
enable them to enact suitable legislation for regulation and control 
of ground water development. 
(iv) Organisation of 187 mass awareness programmes and 118 
training courses on rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge of 
ground water. 
(v) Constitution of Central Ground Water Authority under the

Telecommunications, Central Public Works Department and

(c) if so, whether the Central Government have drawn up some action

THE MINISTER OF WATER RESOURCES (SHRI PRIYARANJAN 
DASMUNSI): (a) Yes, Sir. As per Ministry of Rural Development, an area 
of 26,178 Sq. Km. in 8 districts covering 47 Blocks in Orissa is covered 
under Drought Prone Area Programme (DPAP). 
(b) to (d) Water being a State subject, all water resources schemes 
including the schemes meant for drought proofing of drought prone areas 
in the country are planned, formulated, implemented and funded by the 
respective State Governments out of their own resources and as per 
their own priorities. However, with  an objective to accelerate the 
implementation of those projects which are beyond resource capability 
of the States or are in advanced stage of completion, Central Government 
launched an Accelerated Irrigation Benefits Programme (AIBP) during 
1996-97 to provide Central Loan Assistance (CLA) on matching basis to 
major/medium projects in the country. Priorities are given to those projects 
which are benefiting Tribal and Drought Prone Areas. Since 1999-2000, 
CLA has been provided in the ratio of 3:1 (Centre : State) to Special 
Category States including KBK Districts of Orissa i.e. Kalahandi, Bolangir, 
Naupada and Sonepur, and in the rati o of 2:1 (Centre : State) for the 
projects in rest of the Orissa State. 
With effect from February 2002, AIBP has been linked to economic 
eforms in the irrigation sector and the guidelines have been modified 
accordingly. Since then CLA is being provided to the Reforming States 
under General Category in the ratio of 4:1 (Centre : State) and in the 
ratio of 1:0) (Centre: State) under special category including KBK Districts 
of Orissa, in case they rationalize their water rates in such a way as to 
recover full O & M cost of irrigation projects in 5 years. The State of 
Orissa have been included under the Category of Reforming States. 
So far CLA amounting to Rs. 898.250 crore has been released to 
Government of Orissa. In all, 17 major/medium and 23 Surface Minor 
Irrigation (Ml) Schemes of Orissa have received CLA under AIBP. Out of 
the 17 major/medium irrigation projects, 8 projects are in KBK Districts. 
These 8 projects and 23 Surface Water Ml Schemes have received CLAof

In order to bridge the gap between potential created and that utilized

Bank?

(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) and (b) Reserve Bank of India (RBI)

directions since 4th June, 2004 under section 35A of Banking Regulation Act,

prevent preferential treatment, which was required to protect the interest of the

irregularities and deficiencies of the bank. In view of this, the 
Commissioner of Co-operation and-Registrar of Co-operative Societies 
(RCS), Maharashtra was requisitioned to supersede the Board of Directors 
in May, 2004. The Board was superseded and Administrator was appointed on 
June 5,2004. The RCS was advised on 2.6.2004 to fix accountability in respect

affairs of the bank and take appropriate action.

agriculture, particularly irrigation and infrastructure to reinforce the 
campaign against poverty and unemployment;

revenue deficit, coupled with substantial decrease in domestic savings due

GDP for enhanced public investment without undermining fiscal prudence.

education and health, and facilitating their full participation in the growth process,

eliminating poverty and unemployment. It will also reinforce the growth process,

2143. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) what are the reasons for the difference between the lending rates of 
public sector banks and private sector banks; 
(b) whether the difference between minimum and maximum interest 
rates for demand loans has widened; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) The lending rates of scheduled 
commercial banks have been deregulated by RBI since October, 1994, 
subject to the condition that banks have to declare their Prime Lending Rates 
(PLRs), as approved by their Boards. For credit limits up to Rs. 2 lakh, 
PLR remains the ceiling rate. The PLR is generally fixed by the banks 
taking into account inter-alia, their cost of funds, operational cost, risk 
capital requirements etc. Since April 2001, commericalbanks have been 
given freedom to lend at sub-PLR rates tocreditworthy borrowers on the 
basis of a transparent and objective policy approved by their Boards. 
(b) and (c) RBI has reported that the spread between the maximum and 
minimum lending rates widened between March 2003 and March 2004, 
although there is a general decline in lending rates, both for demand and term 
loans. However, the decline is sharper for public sector banks (PSBs) vis-a-vis 
private sector banks. The range of lending rates for various banks groups for

Waiver of interest on crop loans 
2145. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) the decision of Government regarding waiver of interest to farmers 
on their kharif 2002 crop loans and full re-imbursement thereof by the 
Central Government, as announced earlier in view of wide-spread drought 
and in view of NABARD not implement ing Government assurances of 
total waiver of interest specially in Andhra Pradesh; and 
(b) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) and (b) Considering the severe 
drought during the Kharif 2002, Hon'ble Prime Minister announced in 
the parliament on 18th December, 2002 to convert the short term Kharif 
crop loan, 2002 along with its interest into 4/5 years term loan and to 
waive of first year deferred liability of interest subject to a maximum of 
20% of total interest as a one-time measure to mitigate the hardship 
of drought affected farmers. AS a follow up, RBI vide their circular 
dated 27th December, 2002 advised all scheduled commerical banks 
83 

RAJYA SABHA [24 A ugust, 2004] 
accordingly and NABARD did the same for Regional Rural Banks and 
Cooperative Banks. 
NABARD has already reimbursed Rs. 9.92 crore towards the interest 
waived by 14 Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) in the State of Andhra 
Pradesh under the scheme announced by the Government of India. As 
regards Cooperatives, the State Government of Andhra Pradesh had its 
own scheme to waive of 100% interest on Kharif 2002 crop loans, 
provided the farmers repay the pr incipal. Since the scheme envisaged 
repayment of principal, the Cooperative Banks had not extended term loan 
conversion facility to the farmers and hence were not eligible for 
reimbursement of even the first year  deferred interest liability waived 
by them.

Revised inspection system for Banks 
2155. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR: Will the Minister of FINANCE 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Reserve Bank of India proposes to 
implement the revised inspection system for banks after shifting to the Risk 
Based Supervision (RBS) system; 
93 

RAJYA SABHA [24 August, 2004] 
(b) whether in the proposed RBS system, the supervisory tools will focus 
on greater off site surveillance and targeted on-site inspections; and 
(c) if so, the advantages of revised inspection system? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. As per 
announcement made by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in its monetary and 
credit policy statement for 2000-01, RBI has developed an overall plan for 
monitoring towards Risk Based Supervision (RBS). The basic tool for 
RBS system would be risk profile templates prepared by the banks and 
vetted by RBI. The risks are segregated into eight inherent business risks 
and four control risks, based on the risk matrix of individual bank. RBS 
will focus on targeted on-site inspections depending upon the overall risk 
of individual risk parameters of the said bank, level of risk etc. In addition 
to targeted on-site monitoring, banks are subjected to continuous 
monitoring through off-site surveillance mechanism. 
(c) RBS would benefit the supervisor (RBI) and the supervised entities 
(banks). The adoption of RBS would lead to deeper understanding of the 
risks faced by banks and thereby, facilitate optimum use of scarce 
supervisory resources and direct s upervisory attention to those banks 
and those areas within the banks, which cause more supervisory concern. 
RBS ensure prompt compliance with the regulatory and supervisory 
requirements of RBI. It would also be nefit banks in two ways, first, it 
would enhance the bank's own capability for risk management and risk 
control and second, it will provide a built in incentive of lesser supervisory 
intervention for the good performer.

Home loan fraud cases 
2172. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of 
FINANCE be pleased to state: 
(a) whether several home loan frauds have been reported in banks 
recently; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) the steps taken to co-ordinate among all banks and registrar's 
office to counter the menace of frauds in home loans? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI S.S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) According to the information furnished by the Reserve Bank of 
India, the details of fraud in home loans involving amount of Rs. One crore 
111 

RAJYA SABHA [24 A ugust, 2004] 
and above during the last three years are as under: 
 
Calender Year No. of frauds Amount in crore 
2002 3 8.24 
2003 7 35.34 
2004 (up to June) 1 5.81 
The modus operandi observed in the fraud cases involved one or 
more of the following methods- 
• The same property was offered as security to different banks by 
submitting fake title deeds. 
• The properties, which were mortgaged to the banks, were found 
to be fictitious/non existent. 
• Loans were granted to persons without verifying their whereabouts/ 
details. Such persons were subsequently found to be non-existent. 
• The documents such as title deeds, income tax returns, salary 
certificates etc. submitted for availing the loans were found to be 
fake/fictitious. 
• The Chartered Accountants who had issued/verified the documents 
were found to be fake/non-existent themselves. 
• In a number of fraud cases, the builders/developers had defrauded 
the banks by pocketing the housing loans which they managed to 
obtain in the names of fictitious persons by submitting forged 
documents. 
(c) The steps initiated by RBI to counter the menance of frauds in 
home loans are given below: 
(i) RBI requested all State Governments to computerize land records 
in the sub-Registrar's office to check/avoid multiple charges. State 
Governments were also requested for setting up a "Control 
Registry" which would enable lendi ng institutions to check the 
charges on the property/valid title on the property at the 
Government/Registration Office. 
(ii) All fraud cases involving amounts of Rupees one crore and above 
are followed up by Fraud Monitoring Cell, of RBI. Caution advices 
in respect of builders/unscrupulous borrowers availing home loans 
are issued on receipt of such fraud reports from banks. 
112 

[24 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA  
(iii) Fraud involving amounts of Rs. one lakh and above and upto Rs. one 
crore are monitored by Regional Offices of RBI. 
(iv) Frauds below Rs. one lakh are reported by commercial banks in a 
consolidated manner to RBI at quarterly intervals. 
(v) RBI has advised banks to carry out field level inspections at 
branches having large exposure in home loans. 
(vi) The bank officials are called for discussions at Department of Banking 
Supervision (DBS) of RBI on the issues relating to frauds to impress upon 
them the need for preventive steps to be taken for minimizing frauds 
in housing bans. 
(vi) Wherever necessary, the banks have also lodged complaints with 
Police/CBI/Criminal complaints in court of law in the cases of fraud to 
deter people and employees from indulging in fraudulent activities.

External debt 
2174. SHRIMATI S.G INDIRA: Will the Minister of FINANCE be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that in December, 2003, India's external debt 
stood at U.S. dollar 112.1 billion up by U.S. dollar 6.8 billion over the level of 
end December, 2002; 
(b) whether it is also a fact that the decision to do away with two 
popular NRI schemes resulted in this increase; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; and 
(d) whether Government are considering to re-introduce Non-Resident 
(Non-repatriable) Rupee Deposit and the Non-Resident Special Rupee 
Deposit Scheme? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF FINANCE 
(SHRI  S. S. PALANIMANICKAM): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) and (c) The increase in the external debt was mainly due to the 
surge in the NRI deposits. One of the reasons for the increase in the NRI 
deposits was the discontinuation of the Non-Resident (Non-repatriable) 
Rupee Deposit [NR(N R)RD] scheme with effect from April 1,2002, which partly 
resulted in the higher inflows into the Non-Resident (External) Rupee Account 
[NR(E)RA] as the maturity proceeds of the [NR(NR)RD] were allowed to be 
credited to the [NR (E)RA]. Under the existing practice for compilation of 
external debt statistics, the deposits under the [NR(NR)RD] scheme did not form 
part of external debt, as the principal amount under the scheme was not 
repatriable. However, on discontinuation of this scheme and the subsequent 
crediting of maturity proceeds of [NR(NR)RD] deposits to the [NR(E)RA], these 
deposits are now reckoned as external debt liabilities. 
(d) No such proposal is under consideration.

class tourists; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF TOURISM 
(SHRIMATI RENUKA CHOWDHURY): (a) Yes, Sir. There is a problem of 
lack of availability of adequate confirmed seats/ berths in rail/coaches, 
airlines and accommodation for domestic tourists during the peak season. 
(b) and (c) Tour packages are structured and operated by private

effective tour packages particularly during the summer holidays are offered 
by India Tourism Development Corporation, Indian Airlines, Delhi Tourism 
and Transportation Development Corp oration Ltd., and Ministry of 
Railways:—

journey/accommodation for domestic tourists through various 
Ashok Travels & Tours (ATT) units spread across the country.

the Government on these packages.

as Indian Airlines Flyaways) which offer the facility of booking Air 
tickets, accommodation under a single window and the cost is 
reasonable. To make the packages affordable, Indian Airlines 
discounts its sector air fares by upto 25%. Also just within the 
cost of air fare, most packages include a 3 night/4 day holiday in 
a good category hotel with breakfast, airport transfer, sightseeing, 
taxes, etc.

been organising tour packages specially during summer holidays 
to various tourist places keeping in view the middle class people

are organised by non-AC luxury buses and accommodation on 
r'oom sharing basis is provided to make the packages more cost

assessed at 1869 BCM. The utilisabte water resources is assessed as 1122

well as ground water. A number of surface and ground water schemes are

Erosion crisis in West Bengal 
2238. SHRI TARINI KANTA ROY:  Will the Minister of WATER 
RESOURCES be pleased to state: 
(a) whether erosion has emerged as a crisis in some parts of West 
Bengal, especially in the Malda-Murshidabad districts; 
(b) whether there has been any demand to declare it as a national 
calamity; and 
(c) what steps are being taken by Government to curb the problem? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF WATER 
RESOURCES (SHRI JAI PRAKASH NARAYANA YADAV): (a) Yes, Sir. 
There are reports of severe bank erosion in some parts of West Bengal 
including Malda and Murshidabad districts. 
(b) Yes, Sir. 
(c) Though the Flood Management including river erosion is a state 
subject, the Government of India is provding assistance to West Bengal 
to tackle this problem through a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) 
which was formulated in January, 2001 for implementing critical anti erosion 
schemes. Under this scheme, an amount of Rs. 28.66 crore has so far 
174 

[24 August, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
been released to West Bengal till 2003-04 for taking up anti erosion 
schemes in Malda and Murshidabad districts. The above scheme is also 
being continued further during 2004-07 for which an amount of Rs. 51.00 
crore has been earmarked for the State of West Bengal as Central share 
to take up the critical anti erosion works at an estimated cost of Rs. 
68.00 crore which interalia include seven nos. of schemes for Malda and 
Murshidabad districts. 
In addition to above Farakka Barrage Project Authorities are also 
undertaking the critical anti-erosion works in and around Farakka Barrage 
Project. Since 9th Plan, an amount of Rs. 38.74 crore has been incurred 
by the project on critical anti erosion works in Malda and Murshidabad 
districts till June, 2004. Futher, a provision of Rs. 8.1 crore has been 
made under the CSS for Farakka Barrage Project to take up anti erosion 
works on river Ganga/Padma within its jurisdiction during 2004-07 with 
100% Central funding. 
In order to look into the flood & erosion problem in Assam & 
neighbouring States as well as Bihar, West Bengal and Eastern Uttar 
Pradesh, Government of India have constituted a Task Force in August 
2004 which has been asked to submit their report in a time bound manner.
